summary: Chimbu Airport (CMU) serves Kundiawa, the capital of Papua New Guinea's Chimbu Province, perched in the rugged central highlands at roughly 1,600 meters above sea level. The airport provides a vital air link for one of PNG's most geographically challenging provinces, where road travel is slow and often unreliable due to mountainous terrain. It functions primarily as a domestic hub connecting the highlands region to Port Moresby and other major centers.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly into Chimbu Airport?
A: Air Niugini and PNG Air operate scheduled domestic flights primarily connecting Kundiawa to Port Moresby, with occasional services to other highland destinations.

Q: Is Chimbu Airport suitable for large aircraft?
A: No, the airport has a short runway and is limited to smaller turboprop aircraft such as the Dash 8 and similar highland-capable planes.

Q: How high is Chimbu Airport?
A: The airport sits at a highland elevation of approximately 1,600 meters (5,250 feet) above sea level, which affects aircraft performance and scheduling.

Q: Are there customs or immigration facilities at CMU?
A: No, Chimbu is a domestic-only airport with no international or border control facilities.
transport_tips: Taxis and PMV (public motor vehicle) buses are typically available just outside the small terminal to transport passengers into Kundiawa town, roughly 10-15 minutes away. Due to winding mountain roads, allow extra travel time if continuing onward to other highland towns. Arranging pickup through a local contact or lodge in advance is recommended, as vehicle options can be limited.
local_tip: Flights to and from Chimbu are frequently delayed or rescheduled due to unpredictable mountain weather, so build at least a full day's buffer into any connecting travel plans from this airport.
